h1:
🍢 Best Michelin Isan (Northeastern)
Isan Food, the Michelin Way
intro: Isan is Thailand's boldest, most fearless cooking, and the Michelin inspectors chased it right back to the source. Nine Bib Gourmand kitchens make up this group, led by Krua Khun Nid in Udon Thani and its crisp, tangy fried pla som. From there it is Laab Somphit in Nakhon Ratchasima, turning out proper Yasothon-style laab, koi and nam tok with grilled beef tongue, and Som Tum Jinda in Ubon with its papaya salad topped by fluffy fried catfish.
quickAnswerHtml: This group gathers 9 Bib Gourmand kitchens, led by Krua Khun Nid in Udon Thani and its fried pla som worth pulling over for.

blocks.html: Isan is Thailand's boldest, most fearless cooking, and the Michelin inspectors chased it right back to the source. Nine Bib Gourmand kitchens make up this group, led by Krua Khun Nid in Udon Thani and its crisp, tangy fried pla som. From there it is Laab Somphit in Nakhon Ratchasima, turning out proper Yasothon-style laab, koi and nam tok with grilled beef tongue, and Som Tum Jinda in Ubon with its papaya salad topped by fluffy fried catfish.

blocks.name: Krua Khun Nid
blocks.descHtml:
Krua Khun Nid is open daily 11:00–22:00 (kitchen stops taking orders at 21:00), but there's one important thing to remember: the restaurant is closed on the 20th of every month — never plan a visit on that date. Budget runs around THB 250–500 per person for shared plates, and the more people in your group, the better value it is, since the plates are large and you get to try more dishes. The restaurant is mainly walk-in — no booking needed for two or three people — but if you're coming as a large group, calling ahead to book a table at 042-246128 or 099-442-2962 is safer, since local families pack the place in the evening.

The restaurant sits in a lane beside Wat Pa Non Niwet, on Udon Dutsadi Road, on the western edge of Udon Thani city. It's just a few minutes' drive from the Nong Prajak area — use Wat Pa Non Niwet as your landmark. It's a large restaurant with a comfortable air-conditioned room, and casual dress is fine. The best time to visit is dinner, the way locals do it, or come at lunch if you'd rather avoid the crowds. If you're visiting around the start of the rainy season in June, ask for the ranok mushroom curry or mushroom curry with red ant eggs — seasonal dishes that appear only once a year. Read the full review →
blocks.area: In-town (Mak Khaeng, by Wat Pa Non Niwet)
blocks.cuisine: Traditional Isan food, focused on freshwater fish
mustOrder: Tom yum with Mekong river fish
blocks.bestFor: A family/group meal for freshwater-fish Isan food served family-style, in a comfortable air-conditioned dining room locals actually eat at
blocks.zone: In-town (Mak Khaeng, by Wat Pa Non Niwet)
blocks.foodType: Traditional Isan food, focused on freshwater fish
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Krua Khun Nid official Facebook page

blocks.name: Laab Somphit
blocks.descHtml:
Laab Somphit sits in Trok Chan, off Chan Road, in the middle of Old Korat, not far from the Thao Suranari Monument. Drive or take a songthaew into the old town and walk into the alley from there. The restaurant is open every day from around 07:00 until sometime in the afternoon to evening (sources differ on closing time, anywhere from 16:00 to 19:30 — if you're planning an evening visit, call ahead to check at 044-245-026). No reservations needed — just walk in and sit down.

Price is the main draw. Dishes start at around THB 40, and eating a proper meal runs about THB 100–250 per head, plenty to leave you full. MICHELIN lists the restaurant as cash only (Wongnai says it accepts credit cards), so to be safe, bring cash. The best time to go is late morning to around noon, since special dishes like mum and som neua are made in limited batches and aren't available every day — arrive earlier and you're more likely to find everything on offer. Dishes to make sure are on your table: laab or nam tok made to the Yasothon recipe, grilled beef tongue, grilled sweetbread, and grilled pork neck. Dress is casual, and it's an easy walk into the old town afterward. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Authentic Yasothon-recipe laab-koi-nam tok, with grilled beef tongue and grilled sweetbread
blocks.bestFor: Real Isan laab fans, an Old Korat walking food trail, and anyone looking for great food on a small budget, at Bib Gourmand level

blocks.name: Mekin Farm
blocks.descHtml:
Mekin Farm is in Ban Khok Klang, Chorakhe subdistrict, Nong Ruea district, about 40 kilometres west of downtown Khon Kaen — reachable only by car, roughly 45 minutes to 1 hour. There's parking on the farm. It's open around 09:00–17:30 (some sources say 09:30–17:30, or until 18:00) and closed every Wednesday — remember that before you set off from town. Budget around THB 250–500 per person, and it's cash only according to MICHELIN, so bring enough on you.

Normally you can just walk in, but if you're going as a large group or want to stay at the farmstay (there's only one cottage), call ahead at 061-695-9926 or message the Facebook page "Mekin Farm." Saturdays and Sundays get busy since it's both a cafe and a farm to wander around, so aim to arrive before noon for an easier table and better light for photos in the vegetable and flower plots. Weekdays are much quieter, ideal if you just want to sit and relax. Set aside at least half a day, because after eating there's still the farm, workshops, and the buffalo to say hello to. Read the full review →
blocks.bestFor: Cafe-and-farm lovers, families, and anyone driving around Khon Kaen who wants real farm-to-table food in an Isan countryside setting
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Mekin Farm official Facebook page

blocks.name: Phed Phed Bistro
blocks.descHtml:
Budget about THB 251–500 per person, with most dishes priced THB 100–300 and the famous som tam Luang Prabang at THB 185. You can cross booking off your list entirely, since the Phed Phed group's policy is walk-in only at every branch — the official site phedphed.com spells it out clearly. Call 065-092-9690 or 063-516-5574 with questions, and on days you'd rather not leave the house, order through Grab or LINE MAN instead.

The restaurant is open daily 10:30–21:30, on the G floor in the Forest Trail zone of The Circle Ratchaphruek, in the Taling Chan area. The key thing to know: there's no BTS or MRT nearby — the nearest station is several kilometres away — so the easiest way in is by car (the mall has free parking) or by taxi/Grab. With only about 11–40 seats, the queue builds fast over weekend lunch, so aim to arrive before 11:30 or shift your visit to after 14:00 for a much shorter wait. Dress is casual, no need to overthink it. Read the full review →
blocks.area: The Circle Ratchaphruek community mall (G floor, Forest Trail zone), Bang Ramat, Taling Chan — west Bangkok
blocks.signature: Som tam Luang Prabang (THB 185) with grilled Isan-sourced meats, five spice levels to choose from, big shareable portions
mustOrder: Pork belly fried with fish sauce
blocks.stayLabel: Hotels in good locations in Bangkok
blocks.bestFor: A bold Isan feast for a group of friends or family on the Thonburi side who want a Bib Gourmand restaurant with no booking and no big bill
blocks.zone: The Circle Ratchaphruek community mall (G floor, Forest Trail zone), Bang Ramat, Taling Chan — west Bangkok

blocks.name: Praprai
blocks.descHtml:
Praprai sits in the Ban Phet area, right by the entrance to Khon Kaen airport, about 300 meters from the airport gate — an easy walk. Budget runs 101–250 THB per person (MICHELIN rates it ฿฿). It's walk-in only, no advance booking, with hours roughly 11:00–21:00, closed Mondays — though Wongnai shows it open only on certain days from 11:00–20:00, so it's worth calling ahead to confirm at 081-974-9853 or 043-055287, especially if you're planning to stop by before a flight.

An important tip if you're on a flight schedule: some Wongnai reviews mention food coming out slowly when the restaurant is busy, so build in extra time before your flight to avoid the stress. Lunch and evenings on Friday-Sunday get especially busy since it's a popular stop for travelers passing through — if you'd rather eat at a relaxed pace, go in the early afternoon lull instead. If getting to the restaurant isn't convenient, delivery is available through Wongnai x LINE MAN. Dress is casual. Follow the restaurant on Facebook: prapraikhonkaen Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Fried fermented fish with a perfect sour-salty balance, topped with crispy fried herbs
blocks.bestFor: An Isan meal before your flight at Khon Kaen airport, or your first meal the moment you land
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Praprai Khon Kaen official Facebook page

blocks.name: Prasit
blocks.descHtml:
Prasit Pochana sits on Amat Road, right in downtown Khon Kaen (near the old trading district, just a few minutes' drive from Kaen Nakhon Lake). It's only open from morning to early afternoon, 09:30-14:00, and closed every Monday — worth repeating that this restaurant only sells for half the day. If you're planning to go for dinner, you'll be out of luck. It's a small shophouse restaurant, walk-in only, no table bookings — but there's one important exception: grilled beef tongue needs to be reserved ahead by phone at 043-239-740, since it's made in a limited batch and sells out fast. Michelin itself notes this in the guide.

Budget sits at ฿฿ per Michelin, but in practice most dishes run tens to low hundreds of baht. Two people eating well, ordering a full table, will land somewhere in the high hundreds to low thousands of baht. Cash only, so come prepared. The best time to go is before noon, since customers keep streaming in and the best dishes sell out gradually, especially the deep-fried sun-dried beef and the grilled beef tongue. Dress is casual — whether you show up as a tourist or an office worker, you'll blend right in with the locals. Read the full review →
mustOrder: Grilled beef tongue (call ahead to reserve)
blocks.bestFor: Lunch in downtown Khon Kaen, charcoal-grilled beef fans, and anyone tracking down a Bib Gourmand on a light budget
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Prasit Pochana Khon Kaen official Facebook page

blocks.name: So Jeng
blocks.descHtml:
So Jeng sits on Chaeng Sanit Road in the middle of Ban Phai district, about 44 kilometres from downtown Khon Kaen, roughly a 40-minute drive. Open daily 08:00-21:00 (per MICHELIN; some local sources list 10:00-22:00, so if you're heading there very early or late, call ahead to be sure — 043-274-031 or 087-856-6877). Prices sit at ฿฿ per MICHELIN, working out to a few hundred baht per person, and the restaurant takes cash only, so come prepared.

It's walk-in only, no reservations — but don't worry about the queue, since this is a family-style shophouse restaurant that seats large groups comfortably, and there's a second Ban Phai branch nearby if the original is full. It suits self-drive travellers best, since Ban Phai sits right on the main route heading into southern Isan. Weekday lunch or dinner tends to be less packed — just walk in and order larb neua, koi neua, and tom saep with beef offal without much of a wait. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Larb neua (beef larb) · Koi neua (raw beef koi) · Tom saep neua (beef & offal hot-sour soup)
mustOrder: Tom saep neua (beef & offal hot-sour soup)
blocks.bestFor: Real beef larb-koi fans, big families road-tripping through Isan, and anyone craving a MICHELIN pick on a budget
blocks.libCredit: Photo: So Jeng Pochana (Ban Phai) official Facebook page

blocks.name: Som Tum Jinda
blocks.descHtml:
Som Tum Jinda sits in the heart of Ubon Ratchathani on Phichit Rangsan Road, directly across from Lai Thong Hotel — easy to find, just a few minutes by car or ride-hail from the town center. Open daily 10:30–20:00 (some sources list it open until 21:00 — worth calling ahead to check at 045-255-223). It doesn't take bookings; it's walk-in only, but the restaurant is large, air-conditioned, and turns tables quickly, so waits are usually short — except around the lunch hour on holidays, when it gets especially busy. Build in a little extra wait time, or arrive before 11:30 for a calmer visit.

The budget is very light, around 100–250 THB per person. Order som tam pla duk fu, som tam pu pla ra, laab ped, and grilled chicken with the house dipping sauce to fill the table comfortably without straining the wallet. One important thing to know: the restaurant takes cash only, so withdraw money before you arrive. Dress is casual. It works well as a lunch stop before walking around Thung Si Mueang, or an early dinner before the restaurant closes at eight. Anyone visiting Ubon during the Candle Festival should allow extra time, since the whole city gets busier than usual. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Som tam pla duk fu (crispy catfish floss som tam)
mustOrder: Grilled chicken with house dipping sauce
blocks.bestFor: A full-flavor Isan meal in the middle of Ubon, family-friendly and easy on the budget
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Som Tum Jinda official Facebook page

faq.q: Which Isan restaurant in this group should I try first
faq.a: Krua Khun Nid in Udon Thani sits at the top of the list, and its fried pla som is the dish to order: sour, fragrant and crisp in all the right measures. If you are closer to Korat, Laab Somphit is the other easy call, cooking Yasothon-style laab, koi and nam tok.

faq.q: What is the one dish I have to eat here
faq.a: For a single pick, make it the laab, koi and nam tok at Laab Somphit, served with grilled beef tongue and sweet grilled liver. Som tum lovers should not miss the fluffy fried-catfish papaya salad at Som Tum Jinda in Ubon, or the Luang Prabang som tum at Phed Phed Bistro in Bangkok.

faq.q: Is there an Isan spot from this group in Bangkok
faq.a: Yes, Phed Phed Bistro. It plates a Luang Prabang som tum at 185 baht alongside grilled Isan ingredients, sized large to share around the table, with five levels of heat so you can dial the spice from gentle to serious.

faq.q: Where do I go for Isan-style beef
faq.a: So Jeng in Khon Kaen is the beef specialist, doing beef laab, beef koi and tom saeb with beef and offal. Prasit, also in Khon Kaen, is known for its fried sun-dried beef. Both carry a Bib Gourmand.

faq.q: Which province has the most Isan restaurants in this group
faq.a: Khon Kaen leads with four: Mekin Farm, Praprai, Prasit and So Jeng. The rest are spread across Udon Thani, Nakhon Ratchasima, Ubon Ratchathani and Bangkok.
